Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the Nexara Cloud Q2 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the presentation, we will conduct a question-and-answer session. To ask a question during this time, please press star then the 1 key on your touchtone phone. If you're using a speakerphone, please pick up your handset before pressing the keys. If at any time your question has been addressed and you would like to withdraw it, please press star then the 2 key. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us. Today, we will be discussing Nexara Cloud's results for the second quarter of fiscal 2024. With me on the call are Javier Ramirez, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Kline, Chief Financial Officer; and Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call contains forward-looking statements. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Javier Ramirez.

Javier Ramirez:
Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. Nexara Cloud had a strong Q2, driven by continued growth in our cloud platform and increasing adoption of our AI-powered services.

During the quarter, we focused on four key areas:
1. Expanding our global infrastructure.
2. Enhancing our platform security.
3. Driving innovation in AI and machine learning.
4. Strengthening our partnerships.

Let me elaborate on our global infrastructure expansion, which remains central to scaling for the surging demand in AI and cloud workloads. We've deployed significant capital expenditures to build out capacity ahead of the curve. In fiscal 2024 so far, we've invested $10.8 billion in CapEx, hitting the upper end of our initial guidance and up 28% from last year. This funded $6.2 billion in data center builds and upgrades, $2.8 billion in compute like GPU clusters and our Nimbus AI accelerators, and $1.8 billion in networking and storage. We've boosted global compute capacity by 35% to over 15 exaFLOPS, keeping pace with top hyperscalers.

For fiscal 2025, we're upping our CapEx guide to $16 to $18 billion, a 48% to 67% jump, backed by a $25 billion pipeline of AI contracts from customers like OpenAI and Fortune 100 firms. Q4 2024 CapEx will be $4.2 to $4.5 billion, ramping to $4.5 to $4.8 billion in Q1 2025 for major projects. Breaking it down: 60-65% or $10 to $11.5 billion goes to data centers—$4.5 billion in the Americas for Virginia, Ohio, Texas, and California sites adding 1.5 GW IT load with liquid cooling for H100 and Blackwell GPUs; $3 billion in EMEA for Frankfurt, Paris, and a 300 MW Swedish campus with full renewables for GDPR compliance; and $2.5 billion in APAC for Singapore, Tokyo, and Mumbai to tap India's digital boom and 5G growth.

Compute gets 20-25% or $3.5 to $4 billion, deploying 100,000+ NVIDIA H100/H200 GPUs and 50,000 Nimbus Tensor Cores for 1.5x better TCO, plus quantum-resistant crypto pilots. Networking, storage, and edge take 10-15% or $2 to $2.5 billion, including 800Gbps optics, subsea cables like Apricot, and 50 new edge sites in LATAM and MENA for 5G private clouds.

These moves target AI dominance with 40% GPU utilization, sustainability leadership aiming for 70% renewables by 2026 and carbon-negative by 2030 via Ørsted and NextEra deals, and geopolitical resilience with 25% CapEx in friend-shore regions. Payback is quick at 18-24 months thanks to 85% utilization and premium AI pricing, financed by $8 billion green bonds and $5 billion cash flow, keeping net debt to EBITDA under 1.5x. This builds our moat for 25%+ AI cloud share and 20-25% EPS growth.

Now I'll turn the call over to Sarah Kline to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Sarah Kline:
Thank you, Javier. As Javier mentioned, we had a strong financial performance in the Q2. Revenue grew by 25% year-over-year to $14.2 billion. Our gross margin was 72%, and our operating margin was 28%.

Before diving deeper into the numbers, let me highlight one of our key strategic pillars: energy efficiency and sustainability initiatives. In the hyperscale cloud arena, where we go toe-to-toe with AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud, sustainability drives efficiency, compliance, and customer loyalty. Our enterprise customers—from Fortune 500 financial and healthcare players to AI builders on Nexara AI Fabric—increasingly require proven green metrics. Last quarter, 68% of new large contracts had sustainability SLAs, up from 42% a year ago.

Key progress: Q2 enterprise PUE averaged 1.12 across 28 global data centers, a 15% YoY improvement and better than UHGBC's 1.18 Tier IV benchmark—meaning over 89% energy goes to IT. This came from Phase II direct-to-chip liquid cooling in Virginia and Frankfurt, cutting cooling energy 40% vs. air systems; we're now 65% liquid-cooled, targeting 85% by FY24 end.

Renewables hit 92% matching per RE100 with hourly verification via Ørsted and NextEra partnerships, backed by 2.3 GW PPAs including 1.1 GW new solar in Texas and Rajasthan. Scope 1&2 emissions fell 28% YoY to 1.45 million metric tons CO2e; Scope 3 dropped 12% via Carbon Optimizer migrating idle VMs to low-carbon areas. WUE improved to 0.18 L/kWh from 0.25, using closed-loop towers and AI water recycling in Phoenix.

By region: North America (52% of revenue) has US East/West at 100% renewables, aligning with California SB 100 for 8-12% TCO edge in AI training; offset 450 GWh with batteries like Google's Nevada setup. Europe (28% revenue) tackles CSRD and carbon taxes with Frankfurt/Dublin at 100% hydro/wind, PUE 1.09 vs. Azure's 1.15; €250 million in hydrogen backups with Siemens for EEG exemptions. APAC (22% YoY growth to $3.1 billion) features Singapore/Tokyo at 95% renewables and Chennai's 500 MW immersion-cooled site slashing GPU energy 30%, offering Green Zones 20% lower carbon than Alibaba.

These efforts boost margins—$285 million opex savings last year added 220 bps to gross margins—and we pass 40% savings via Sustainable Compute, up 145% QoQ. Nexara One now includes Workload Carbon Footprinting API for Kubernetes/Terraform devs. We're aiming net-zero Scope 1&2 by 2028 with $1.2 billion capex for quantum-dot LEDs, neuromorphic chips, and Pachama blockchain credits.

As AI eats 8-10% global power by 2026 per IEA, efficient providers win; our scorecard secured 14 of 20 hyperscale RFPs. Full ESG details next month.

Now, I'll hand it back to Javier for further comments.

Javier Ramirez:
Thank you, Sarah. We are particularly excited about the momentum we are seeing with Nexara AI Fabric, which is driving significant total cost of ownership savings and rapid deployment for our customers.

Turning to these new service launches and their outstanding market reception, they've supercharged our growth. New services added $450 million in Q2—16% of our $14.2 billion total revenue—up 320% YoY. This positions us in Gartner's $679 billion cloud market driven by AI, edge, and hybrid/multi-cloud.

Our big launches: Nexara AI Fabric for gen AI orchestration; EdgeForge Secure for edge computing; and GreenCloud Optimizer for carbon management—all backed by $1.2 billion FY2023 R&D in Kubernetes 1.29 and Apache Iceberg.

Nexara AI Fabric, launched January, offers managed fine-tuning, scalable inference, and RAG with our 100PB vector DB at sub-10ms latency, supporting Hugging Face, Llama 3, Claude—cutting inference costs 40-60% vs. SageMaker or Azure ML. Q2 brought 2,800 customers including a Fortune 50 bank shifting $750 million GPU spend; $280 million new ARR, 135% NRR, 75% production in 48 hours. NPS 78, 52% TCO savings vs. on-prem; 12% NA AI PaaS share per Synergy, gaining on Vertex AI. NA 65%, APAC 450% YoY, EMEA bank wins.

EdgeForge Secure, March launch, delivers edge nodes at 150+ PoPs with 5G slicing, ZTNA, confidential compute (SGX/SEV-SNP), 99.9999% uptime, <5ms latency for IoT/5G/AR. $110 million revenue from 1,200 customers at 85% margins via Equinix/DR partners; 0.2% churn, 40% paired with AI Fabric like automaker's 2TB/hr AV data. Beats Akamai/Fastly on K8s; Verizon/Vodafone 5G pilots for $200 million potential. EMEA 42%, APAC 30%, NA gaming/retail.

GreenCloud Optimizer, May SaaS, uses ML for low-carbon placement across clouds, CSRD/SEC compliant. $60 million from 950 users, 28% carbon/15% cost cuts, 22% referrals; retailer win cut emissions 40%. 18% sustainable tool share per IDC.

These align with "Cloud Native Everywhere," growing RPO to $18.5 billion (+42% YoY, 65% from new). GPU mitigations, 22% op margins. Q3 new services $600 million, 4,000 AI Fabric logos, new PoPs in Jakarta/São Paulo for 30% APAC/LATAM growth.

We continue to invest in research and development to stay ahead of the curve in the rapidly evolving cloud landscape. Our commitment to innovation is reflected in our recent advancements in multi-cloud and hybrid cloud capabilities.

Let me update you on these partnership initiatives, a growth cornerstone amid the shift to multi-cloud/hybrid setups. Gartner notes 92% enterprises multi-cloud, up from 85%, for lock-in avoidance, TCO, AI/sovereignty.

Q2 multi/hybrid revenue up 48% YoY to $1.2 billion (32% total), RPO $4.8 billion (+55%), 128% NRR, 1,200 customers +150 logos.

Partnerships shine: AWS Fabric Connector for EKS/ECS/Outposts orchestration; 62% joint wins like financial firm's 28% TCO save on VMware migration; $150 million GTM co-invest for AI with Bedrock/AetherML.

Azure Arc Harmony GA for Arc HCI/AKS; 75% top-50 adoption, 35% egress savings for auto OEM; 70% QoQ bookings, sovereign extensions.

Google Anthos UniOrchestrator (Istio/Knative) for GKE/AKS/EKS; 40% shift to Distributed Cloud Edge, telco win cut deploys to hours, 99.99% uptime.

Post-VMware, Tanzu Bridge for vSphere migrations; 200+ shifts, $250 million pipeline, 25-30% cost cuts.

OCI for Exadata DBs (85% portability), Red Hat OpenShift operators, Dell APEX HCI for edge.

Regions: APAC 72% penetration, $420 million (+65%); EMEA hybrid ARR $310 million (+52%); Americas 55%, LatAm via AWS.

New: UniCloud Fabric 2.0 intent networking (Terraform/Pulumi/Crossplane), 40% faster provision, 99.999% SLA; Hybrid AI Accelerator for NVIDIA DGX federated learning, 3x training speed, 22% lower GPU costs.

We're the neutral orchestrator, $500 million R&D for zero-trust/green; 35% lower carbon. Q4 50% growth, $2 billion RPO add-ons.

With that, let's open the call for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, if you would like to register a question, please press star then the 1 key on your touchtone phone. Our first question comes from Ben Thompson with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Ben Thompson:
Thanks, and congrats on a solid quarter. Javier, on the global infrastructure buildout, can you talk more about how you're prioritizing regions amid supply chain risks and the CapEx ramp? Specifically, any shifts in allocation?

Javier Ramirez:
Thanks, Ben. Absolutely, prioritization is key. As I outlined, we're balancing AI demand with resilience—25% of new CapEx in friend-shore areas to dodge U.S.-China chip tensions from TSMC. Americas get the lion's share for our AI hubs like Ohio, but EMEA and APAC expansions ensure sovereign compliance and growth capture. Utilization is already 85%+, so this secures supply for hyperscale RFPs. We're on track for payback in under two years.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen:
Great, thanks. Sarah, the multi-cloud segment growth is impressive at 48%. With hyperscaler consolidation, how do you see partnerships evolving, and any update on RPO conversion there?

Sarah Kline:
Hi Lisa, thanks. Partnerships are our interoperability edge—deep AWS, Azure, Google integrations like Fabric Connector and Arc Harmony have driven 62% and 70% joint bookings growth. Post-VMware, Tanzu Bridge accelerated $250 million pipeline. RPO at $4.8 billion converts at 45-50% to revenue, with 128% NRR signaling expansions. Q4 guides to 50% segment growth, $2 billion add-ons, as enterprises bet on neutral platforms amid AI/data rules.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Raj Patel with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Raj Patel:
Thanks for taking my question. Elena, on the new services like AI Fabric and EdgeForge, what's the early feedback on integration with open-source ecosystems, and competitive moats?

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Raj, great question. Feedback is stellar—AI Fabric's Kubernetes-native RAG and vector DB hit 75% production in 48 hours, 135% NRR, beating SageMaker on TCO. EdgeForge's Operators enable 25% faster deploys vs. Akamai, with 99.9999% uptime for 5G. Our open integrations—Terraform, Prometheus, Istio—build stickiness; NPS 78, near-zero churn. Moat is composability: 40% GPU efficiency, green optimizations, positioning us as #3 in hybrid with 14% share.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Maria Gonzalez with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Maria Gonzalez:
Thanks. Javier, sustainability was detailed—impressive PUE and renewables. How does this factor into customer RFPs and margins going forward?

Javier Ramirez:
Maria, spot on. Sustainability won 14 of 20 hyperscale RFPs; 68% new contracts demand SLAs. PUE 1.12 and 92% renewables give 8-12% TCO edge, saving $285 million opex last year for 220 bps margin lift. We're passing 40% via Sustainable Compute (145% QoQ), targeting net-zero 2028. It's a moat as AI power surges—customers like Anthropic prioritize us.

Javier Ramirez:
Thank you for your questions and your continued support. We are confident in our ability to continue to deliver strong results and create long-term value for our shareholders.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the call.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
